body: The highest-risk combination in the case record is an **auditor resignation, plus preferential issues, plus loud promoter communication, plus finfluencer hype, plus a rising pledge**. Regulators do not always conclude fraud. SEBI closed its Hindenburg proceedings against Adani in September 2025, finding the allegations "not established" ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/markets/news/sebi-clears-adani-group-dismisses-hindenburg-allegations-125091801259_1.html)). A retail investor does not need a regulator's burden of proof, though. **Doubt is a sufficient reason to pass.** Standard scoring tools, the Beneish M-score (above −1.78 suggests manipulation risk), the Altman Z-score and the Piotroski F-score, are useful as overlays, but the research found no validation of them on Indian data.

`event:ketan-parekh-tech-2000` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, blowup, fraud, sector-it, cyclical

Sensex peaked at ~6,150 intraday on 11 Feb 2000 (level from memory; not confirmed in sources found) and fell to ~2,600 by Sept 2001 (post-9/11 low) - roughly -58%. What led: 'ICE' (information technology, communications, entertainment) and Ketan Parekh's 'K-10' stocks - Zee Telefilms (reportedly ~Rs 127 to ~Rs 10,000 pre-split), HFCL, Global Tele-Systems, DSQ Software, Pentamedia, Aftek, Silverline. Parekh funded positions via Madhavpura Mercantile Cooperative Bank and Global Trust Bank, plus 'badla' carry-forward financing. In the two months after April 2000, K-10 stocks fell ~67% vs -23% for the Sensex (student document; weak source); for the year to Feb 2002 the K-10 averaged -51.7% vs -16% for the Sensex (Business Standard). A bear-cartel raid and the Feb 2001 budget triggered the March 2001 crash; MMCB collapsed, UTI's US-64 froze (July 2001), badla was banned and rolling settlement introduced. What lagged: 'old economy' stocks that traded at single-digit P/Es (unverified levels). Valuation at peak: Sensex P/E ~28-35x depending on source (28x, 29x, ~35x Apr 2000). Top signals: extreme concentration in one theme, cooperative-bank funding of a broker, triple-digit P/Es on IT names. Lesson: many K-10 names never recovered; theme leaders of one bubble rarely lead the next.

`https://www.nseindia.com/*` now answers with a **301 to `https://www.nseindia.in/*`**. It only does this if the request carries a full browser header set; with fewer headers Akamai returns 403 "Access Denied". Archives are on `nsearchives.nseindia.in` and attachment URLs point there too. The old `nsearchives.nseindia.com` still serves CSVs.
On `www.nseindia.in`, the `/api/corporate*` endpoints work **without a cookie** if you send a browser User-Agent plus `Accept`, `Accept-Language` and `Referer`. That holds over both HTTP/1.1 (so Python `urllib` works) and HTTP/2. A bare curl UA or `Python-urllib` UA gets an HTTP/2 stream reset. `quote-equity` (live prices) stays 403 even after a homepage cookie visit: it is protected by bot-manager. The old `www1.nseindia.com` gives a TLS failure.
